IIT in Andhra Pradesh
*1. SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether his Ministry has considered
the proposal of Andhra Pradesh
Government for establishment of an IIT at
Basara in Adilabad district of Andhra
Pradesh;
(b) if so, the details of the proposal and
the action taken thereon, indicating the
amount sanctioned for this purpose;
(c) whether, on the recommendation of
an expert Committee constituted by
Andhra Pradesh Government, the Union
Government propose to upgrade Osmania
University College of Engineering and
Technology and Andhra Pradesh College
of Engineering to IIT status;
(d) if so, by when; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Power generation by 2020
*2. SHRI DARA SINGH: Will the
Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have the
capacity to generate 21,180 Megawatts of
electricity by 2020, under its calculated
power programme;
(b) whether the Department of Atomic
Energy (DAE) had also submitted certain
proposals in this regard to the Committee
of Secretaries in early December, 2006; and
(c) if so, the number of proposals
examined by the said Committee and what
is the outcome thereof?
Begging by children
†*3. DR. PRABHA THAKUR: Will
the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND
EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the fact that thousands of children in the
country are either engaged in begging or
being used as means of begging;
(b) the steps taken by Government to
protect them from such exploitation;
(c) whether Government are aware that
several anti-social organisations are engaged

innocent children after kidnapping and
make them source of their income by
forcing them to beg; and
(d) the measures taken by Government
to salvage these tiny kids from such in-
human and exploitating situation and
whether these measures have proved to be
effective; if so, the details thereof?
Validity of laws placed in the Ninth
Schedule of the Constitution
*4. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
SHRI AMAR SINGH:
Will the Minister of LAW AND
JUSTICE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
review the Constitution of India in the wake
of recent Supreme Court order which lays
down that all laws placed in the Ninth
Schedule after 1973 would be open to
judicial review;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, in what manner Government
propose to resolve the reservation
policy of Tamil Nadu Government which
has made reservation to the extent of 69
per cent?
Increase in the number of
Anganwadis
*5. SHRI K.E. ISMAIL: Will the
Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Supreme
Court has ordered Government to take
measures to increase the number of
Anganwadis from the present six lakhs to
fourteen lakhs in a phased manner by 2008
in order to realize the commitment made in
the Common Minimum Programme of UPA
Government to universalize the ICDS
Scheme;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
measures being taken by Government;
(c) whether it is a fact that some State
Governments have failed to implement the
earlier orders of the Supreme Court in this
regard; and
(d) if so, which are the States lagging
behind in implementing the ICDS Scheme
and what action is being taken against these
States?
Prestigious educational institutions
in different States
*6. SHRI PYARIMOHAN MOHA-
PATRA: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of Centrally funded
prestigious educational institutions like IIT,
IIM, IIIT and Central Universities
etc., located in different States,
State-wise;
(b) the reasons for not establishing a
single such institution in Orissa over the
last 60 years since Independence;
(c) the norms for establishing such
institutions adopted for the Eleventh Five
Year Plan; and
(d) the reasons for not considering
Orissa as a location inspite of the need to
support the State’s ambitious industrial
development programme as well as
education of nearly 40 per cent tribal and
SC population of the State?

3

Missing children in the country
*7. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND
CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the NHRC report lists
nearly 45000 children going missing every
year in the country;
(b) whether according to the report,
most children are reported missing from
the States where the trafficking of children
has become a highly profitable business;
(c) whether it is also fact that large
number of missing children go untraced;
(d) if so, the State-wise details of cases
of missing children for the last three years;
(e) whether there is any mechanism to
monitor the situation; and
(f) the steps taken to protect the
children?
Improvement in power distribution
after privatization
†*8. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL: Will the Minister of
POWER be pleased to state:
(a) the qualitative improvements that
have emerged in the field of power
distribution as a result of its privatization
in the country;
(b) whether any proposal is being
considered by Government regarding
restructuring of power distribution model
and to encourage lawful competition
amongst existing power companies; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Subsidy to solar water heating system
*9. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B. J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of NEW AND
RENEWABLE ENERGY be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government propose to
provide subsidy to popularise solar water
heaters to conserve energy;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the action plan of Government to
popularise the solar water heating system
in the backward Orissa State, which has
abundant potential in this sector?
Opportunities for professional
education in the country
*10. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether his Ministry’s survey on
opportunities for professional education
in the country reveals that some States are
lagging behind in terms of seat availability
per lakh population and in a
communication to Chief Ministers
suggested to shape up and open new
institutes, increase intake, start new
branches and courses and provide incentives
for starting private institutions;
(b) if so, States that are lagging behind
the national average in terms of educational
opportunities; and
(c) the steps these States have taken to
increase and bring them at least at par with
the national average to remove the regional
disparities?

4
Vice Chancellor in Central Institute
of English and Foreign Languages
*11. SHRI SITARAM YECHURY:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the post of
Vice Chancellor in Central Institute of
English and Foreign Languages is vacant
for long time;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether Government have received
any representation seeking intervention in
the administration; and
(d) whether Government would spell
out a definitive time-frame within which
they can appoint a regular Vice Chancellor?
Power generation through renewable
sources for rural electrification
*12. DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY:
Will the Minister of NEW AND
RENEWABLE ENERGY be pleased to
state:
(a) whether India seeks to double its
power generation capacity by 2012
generating 10,000 MW through renewable
sources mainly for use in rural
electrification;
(b) the number of villages which will be
lighted up using mainly biomass or organic
waste;
(c) the number of villages which have
been lighted up using biomass as on date;
(d) whether any biomass power plants
are being run using wood in any State in
India; and
(e) if so, the steps taken by Government
in this regard?
Malnourished children and ICDS
centres
*13. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will
the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD
DEVELOPMENT be  pleased to state
(a) the ratio of per one lakh
malnourished  children and the number of
ICDS centres in the country, in view of
16.4 crore malnourished children in the age
group of 0—6 years in the country;
(b) the per capita expenditure on
malnourished children in the country and
the amount directly reaching the children
on food; and
(c) the reaction of Government thereto?
Comprehensive legislation for
judicial reforms
*14. DR. P.C. ALEXANDER: Will the
Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE  be
pleased to state whether instead of going
ahead with the proposed Judges Enquiry
Bill, 2006 as an isolated legislation for
ensuring accountability alongwith
independence of the judiciary, Government
will consider a legislation covering all issues
relevant to judicial reforms, such as,
establishment of an All India Judicial
Service, appointment of judges of the
Supreme Court and High Court, etc., and
include enquiry into allegation of
misbehaviour or incapacity against judges
as part of this comprehensive legislation?
Foreign education providers in the
country
*15. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTA-
CHARJEE: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of foreign education

5

the country for higher education and on
what terms and conditions:
(b) whether degrees awarded by these
education providers would be recognised
by Government; and
(c) the cities where such campuses
would be established?
Inquiry into Nithari murders
*16. SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND
CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether a Central panel inquiring
into the Nithari murders has submitted its
report and has suggested widening the scope
of the investigation to cover possibilities
including organ trade and sexual exploitation
and has recommended certain measures to
avoid such incidents in future;
(b) if so, whether her Ministry has
examined the recommendations of the
Committee; and
(c) if so, whether the suggestions made
in the report has been forwarded to the
CBI for further investigation?
Lapses in ICDS implementation
*17. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA: W ill the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Supreme Court on July 19,
2006 appointed a two-member committee
to go into the question of serious lapses in
ICDS implementation and found serious
lapses on the part of both Centre and States;
(b) whether a noted economist releasing
a report based on a survey of the ICDS in
six States in 2004, pointed out the same
position; and
(c) whether the Hon’ble Prime Minister
recently expressed concern over poor
implementation of the scheme and in a
written communication to the Chief
Ministers suggested to set up
institutionalized review process and report
the position to the Centre?
Transfer of technology development
by CFTRI
*18. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the
Minister of SCIENCE AND
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Central Food
Technology Research Institute is claimed
to be the forerunner and leader in food
sciences and food technology;
(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that
most of the technologies developed by
CFTRI are not transferred, not found
suitable for transfer, not invoking interest
of industry, not found satisfactory by
buyers, not economically viable and
transferred by violating CSIR guidelines;
and
(c) whether there are any audit paras in
this regard?
Additional fund under National
Nutrition Mission
*19. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY:
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND
CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Government of Andhra
Pradesh has submitted any proposal for

6

Nutrition Mission;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the steps being taken by
Government to release the above amount
to the State?

SABHARWAL: Will the Minister of
MINES be pleased to state:

have requested the Central Government for
fixing royalty of minerals on ad-valorem
basis;
 (b) whether these State Governments
have also sought the powers from Central
Government to allocate mines of
prospective investors;
(c) if so, the complete details in this
regard and Government’s reaction to the
request of State Governments; and
(d) whether Government are considering
to formulate a policy document on minerals
and if so, the details in this regard?
